Q: Verilog simulation: all outputs x A:

You need to set your testbench reset_n signal to 0 at time 0 to reset your logic. After a delay, you should set reset_n to 1.

Change:

        reset_n = 1; LB = 1; RB = 0;

to:

        reset_n = 0; LB = 1; RB = 0;

All reg signals default to X.

Q: Why should I learn Javascript if I could just learn jQuery? A:

As a long-time stalwart supporter of jQuery myself, I'll say: Learn Javascript.

  • To use jQuery, you need a good grounding in Javascript.
  • To learn Typescript, it helps to have a good grounding in Javascript.
  • To learn Angular, you need a good grounding in Typescript.
  • To use React, you need a good grounding in either Javascript or Typescript.

As others have pointed out, to make your website interactive, you can do it all with Javascript these days.

So why learn jQuery at all at this time? jQuery is succinct. It's quick to write and easy to read. Obviously with IntelliCode and AI coding assistants, even that is becoming less relevant.

Q: Is it better to store data for a modular system in sets of arrays or to use reflection to get the data straight from a class? A:

First, EVERYTHING that you don't need to read from a file is in RAM, that's not an issue. Secondly, it is nearly always a bad idea to use reflection. Use java's ArrayList class.

Q: Evaluating statements with negative numbers in Pascal A:

You need to drop out of the loop before determining the new maximum. If you enter 5 numbers, then you perform 5 value > max tests. That means you consider the input of 0 being part of the sample, too. However, you want to make only N − 1 comparisons.

The quickest solution is to turn your code upside down and rewrite your head‐controlled loop into a tail‐controlled loop. This avoids double‐checking for a value of 0 like MartynA suggested.

The best solution is to abandon the sentinel‐based termination approach altogether and use the built‑in function EOF instead. But take one step at a time, fix your original program first.

PS: There is no need to parenthesize the entire Boolean expression in an if‐statement.

Q: Any Potential Issues With Struct A Being Referenced in Struct B and Vice Versa? A:

While the structures themselves are fine, there might become a problem if you create a circular reference, shallow or deep. Especially if it involves dynamic allocation (it could too easily lead to a situation where pointers to free'd structures are dereferenced).

Q: Problem with CSV import from stage (curly brackets) A:

The file format name is wrong in the copy into ... query.

The file format you created is named as CSV_SEMICOLON_QUOTES_HEADER2. but in your query you wrote ..HEADER instead of ..HEADER2
